//: What staging holds so the e2e suite has something to sign in to.
THE ADDRESS IS NOT HERE, AND MUST NOT BE. This repo is public and
e2e/CLAUDE.md forbids the test user's address in any committed file — not
as a default, not in a fixture, not in a comment. ${E2E_TEST_USER_EMAIL}
is the same environment secret the Playwright run reads, so the firm and
the sign-in cannot drift onto two different people. Loading fails loudly
if it is unset rather than seeding a firm for the empty string.
The account itself is created once by scripts/e2e-create-test-user.sh;
this only puts it in a firm. Seeding is idempotent and runs on every
staging deploy, so if staging's tables are ever recreated the next run
restores this instead of failing a week later as a mystery app regression.
THE SUBJECT IS SUPPLIED, NOT LOOKED UP, and that is a security decision
rather than an optimisation. A Cognito sub is server-minted but constant
once the account exists, so resolving it at seed time buys nothing — and
it would cost the pipeline an AdminGetUser grant that cannot be scoped to
one pool: ci-trust is applied before any pool exists and cannot know their
opaque ids, so the grant would have to be userpool/*, which includes
PROD's pool and therefore customer email addresses. Supplying the value
keeps that grant out of CI entirely. Read it once with
aws cognito-idp admin-get-user --user-pool-id <staging pool> \
--username "$E2E_TEST_USER_EMAIL" \
--query 'UserAttributes[?Name==`sub`].Value' --output text
and store it as the E2E_TEST_USER_SUBJECT environment secret. It is not a
credential, but it identifies a person, so it does not belong in this file
either.
